title: Platform systems & services: guide, runbooks, dashboards, alerts and roadmap
author: Alex Chen
content:
Summary

This doc is the canonical platform engineering reference for systems and services operated by the Platform team. It consolidates the systems inventory, how-tos for common platform tasks, dashboards & alerts standards, runbooks for production incidents, recent retrospectives and the near-term roadmap. Use this page as the single source of truth when oncall-ing, planning platform work, or onboarding new team members.

Sections
1) Overview and systems inventory
2) Ownership, SLOs and escalation paths
3) How-tos (deploy, add alert, create dashboard)
4) Dashboards & alerts standards and examples
5) Runbooks: incident triage & resolution steps
6) Retrospectives — recent incidents and action items
7) Roadmap — priorities for the next two quarters
8) Team wiki, onboarding and links

---

1) Overview and systems inventory

Short intro:
The Platform org operates core services that make Redwood Inference's inference platform reliable and observable. This inventory lists services we own, their purpose, SLOs, and primary owners. Use this table when routing incidents and planning capacity work.

Inventory (columns: service, purpose, critical SLO, owner, pager):
- platform-core: request router and service discovery; SLO: 99.95% p99 request latency < 150ms; owner: Platform Runtime (team-platform-runtime); pager: runtime-oncall@redwood.com
- obs-ingest: metrics and traces ingestion; SLO: 99.9% availability; 95th percentile write latency < 200ms; owner: Observability (team-observability); pager: obs-oncall@redwood.com
- metrics-processor: rollups, SLOs and alert evaluation; SLO: 99.9% evaluation within 60s; owner: Observability; pager: obs-oncall@redwood.com
- kv-cache: global prefix cache for inference; SLO: 99.9% hit availability; owner: Serving Runtime; pager: runtime-oncall@redwood.com
- model-store: model artifacts and versioning storage; SLO: 99.99% object read availability; owner: Model Onboarding; pager: model-oncall@redwood.com
- provisioning: cluster autoscaler and capacity planner; SLO: 99.9% scaling actions within policy windows; owner: Infra Platform; pager: infra-oncall@redwood.com

Service ownership guidance:
- Each service has a primary owner (team) and a 24/7 pager rotation. Team owners are responsible for runbooks, dashboards, and post-incident follow-ups.
- For cross-service incidents, the platform triage lead coordinates via the platform incident channel (#inc-platform).

---

2) Ownership, SLOs and escalation paths

SLO baseline (platform-wide):
- Platform availability (end-to-end request success): 99.9% monthly
- P99 latency for API calls: target <= 150ms for small requests (<= 4k tokens)
- Embedding throughput: target sustained throughput as provisioned per-dedicated pool (documented per-customer)

Escalation matrix (ordered):
1. Pager rotation (primary oncall) — attempt page, acknowledge within 5 minutes for P1
2. Team lead (if no ack in 10 minutes or incident is P0)
3. Platform Engineering Manager and SRE Director (if >30 minutes unresolved or cross-region outage)
4. CTO (for SEV0 business-impacting incidents)

Contact and channel list:
- Primary incident channel: #inc-platform (Slack)
- Pager emails: runtime-oncall@redwood.com, obs-oncall@redwood.com, infra-oncall@redwood.com
- Status page: status.redwood.ai

---

3) How-tos (common tasks)

A. Deploy a platform service (kube, ci/cd)
1. Confirm change in PR with 2 approvers (owner + infra reviewer).
2. Run unit + integration tests locally: `./scripts/test --service platform-core`
3. Submit canary deployment via CI: `ci deploy --service platform-core --canary`
4. Monitor canary for 15 minutes (p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate) on the canary dashboard.
5. Promote to stable when metrics are green and no regressions are seen.
6. If regressions appear, run automatic rollback: `ci rollback --service platform-core --to last-stable`

B. Add an alert to the metrics platform (Prometheus + alertmanager via metrics-processor)
1. Open PR in infra/alerts repo, add rule YAML under `rules/platform/` with a clear summary and runbook link. Example rule header: `- alert: PlatformHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-core",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-core"}[5m])) > 0.02`
2. Include labels: severity: page | ticket, owner_team: team-platform-runtime, runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-core-runbook-2026.json
3. Add dashboard panel and link to the alert in the PR description.
4. Request reviewer from Observability and Platform Runtime.
5. After merge, ensure Alertmanager routing maps page-level alerts to the correct pager.

C. Create a dashboard (Grafana)
1. Use the platform dashboard template (folder: platform-templates) and keep panels focused (no more than 8 per high-level dashboard).
2. Required panels for a service dashboard: Summary (availability, error-rate), Latency (p50/p95/p99), Traffic (rps), Resource usage (CPU/GPU mem) and Alert summary.
3. Document the dashboard purpose in the dashboard description and link the relevant runbook.
4. Add dashboard owners in metadata (view/edit).

---

4) Dashboards & alerts standards and examples

Standards:
- Dashboards should drive action: each panel must map to at least one alert or known troubleshooting step.
- Default time window: 1h for incident triage, 7d for trend analysis.
- Color conventions: green for OK, yellow for warning threshold, red for page-level threshold.
- Alert severities: page (P1/P0), ticket (P2/P3). Page-level alerts must include runbook and paging label.

Example alert thresholds (platform-core):
- High error rate (page): error rate > 2% sustained for 5m -> page runtime-oncall@redwood.com
- Latency regression (ticket): p99 latency > 250ms for 10m -> ticket team-platform-runtime
- Cache eviction storm (page): kv-cache eviction rate > 1000/s for 1m -> page runtime-oncall@redwood.com
- Ingest lag (page): obs-ingest write lag > 30s -> page obs-oncall@redwood.com

Dashboard example (panels):
- Platform Core Overview: availability sparkline, current error rate, p95/p99 latency, active requests, top endpoints by error
- Observability Pipeline: ingestion rate, queue depth, processing latency, alert burn rate
- Cluster Capacity: GPU utilization by pool, pending scheduling, node autoscaler events

---

5) Runbooks: incident triage & resolution steps

General oncall triage procedure (P0/P1):
1. Acknowledge the page within 5 minutes. Post an update to #inc-platform with current hypothesis.
2. Capture impact: affected customers, regions, scale, and business risk.
3. Run quick checks: service health (`kubectl get pods -n platform`), logs (`stern platform-core --since 10m`), metrics panels (overview dashboard).
4. If service is degraded, follow service-specific runbook steps. Example (platform-core degraded):
  a. Check recent deploys: `ci rollout history --service platform-core`
  b. If deploy in last 30m, rollback and observe.
  c. If not deploy-related, examine upstream dependencies (model-store, kv-cache, obs-ingest).
5. Engage owners for dependent services and create an incident document (use template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-template.json).
6. Provide regular updates every 15 minutes until a mitigation is applied.
7. After mitigation, run full recovery checklist and close the page once post-checks are green for 30 minutes.

Post-incident (retrospective) steps:
1. Open a postmortem document within 48 hours. Include timeline, root cause, impact, and actions.
2. Assign owners and due dates for each corrective action.
3. Track actions in the platform sprint board; review status weekly until complete.

Runbook examples (quick links):
- platform-core-runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-core-runbook-2026.json
- obs-ingest-runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/obs-ingest-runbook-2026.json

---

6) Retrospectives — recent incidents and action items

Summary of recent SEVs (last 6 months):
- 2025-12-02 (SEV1) obs-ingest partial outage — root cause: misconfigured Kafka retention leading to backlog. Actions: add retention alert, increase consumer parallelism (done), review Kafka provisioning (in progress).
- 2026-01-18 (SEV0) platform-core latency spike affecting multiple customers — root cause: a rollout with a mis-tuned kernel; Actions: stricter canary gating, add p99 regression alert for deploys (done), add performance test to CI (in progress).

Open action items:
- 2026-02-10: Complete autoscaler policy revamp (owner: Infra Platform, due 2026-04-15)
- 2026-02-18: Finish metrics-processor scale test (owner: Observability, due 2026-03-15)

Retrospective findings:
- Automation gaps during rollback: need a documented and tested rollback playbook in CI for all critical services.
- Observability coverage: add synthetic traffic tests for core endpoints and wire them into dashboards.

---

7) Roadmap — priorities for next two quarters

Goals (2026 Q1-Q2):
- Improve platform reliability: reduce platform-wide P99 latency by 15% across common request patterns.
- Observability hardening: finish metrics-processor scale tests; add synthetic monitors for top-10 endpoints.
- Developer velocity: simplify dashboard creation via a dashboard CLI and template library.
- Cost optimization: intelligent batching pilot to reduce token cost in hosted tiers.

Planned initiatives with owners and rough timeline (table-style bullet list):
- Autoscaler policy revamp (owner: Infra Platform) — Q1 2026 — milestones: design, test, rollout
- Canary performance gating (owner: Platform Runtime) — Q1 2026 — add CI perf tests and deploy gating
- Dashboard CLI (owner: Observability) — Q2 2026 — alpha for internal teams
- Synthetic monitors (owner: Observability) — Q1-Q2 2026 — top-10 endpoints first

How to contribute to the roadmap:
- Create RFCs in the platform RFC board, assign an owner and timeline, and tag `platform-roadmap` label. The platform PM will triage and add to quarterly planning.

---

8) Team wiki, onboarding and links

Onboarding checklist for new platform engineers:
- Read this page and the platform playbook.
- Complete platform runbooks review and sign-off.
- Shadow oncall for two weeks with a buddy.
- Deploy a small non-critical change end-to-end.

Important links:
- Platform Playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026.json
- Oncall template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-template.json
- Dashboard templates folder (Grafana): grafana://platform-templates
- CI/CD docs: /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/

Appendix: Useful commands and scripts
- `kubectl -n platform get pods` — service status
- `stern platform-core --since 10m` — tail recent logs across pods
- `ci deploy --service <name> --canary` — start canary deploy
- `ci rollback --service <name> --to last-stable` — rollback to last stable release

If you find missing owners, incorrect SLOs, or outdated dashboards, please file a small update PR to this page or ping the platform doc owners.
